# `silk/i32`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Profiles: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`.

Thirty-two-bit signed integers and the default type of context-free integer literals.

## When to use

Use `i32` for ordinary signed whole-number calculations whose range is known to fit, and when a
stable 32-bit representation matters. Choose `isize` for pointer-sized offsets and `i64` for a
wider fixed range.

## Details

Ordinary arithmetic, narrowing conversions, division by zero, and invalid shift counts trap.
`checked*` reports invalid arithmetic with [`Option`](./option.md#declaration-73696c6b2f6f7074696f6e3a3a4f7074696f6e); `wrapping*` computes modulo 2^32;
`saturating*` clamps at [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d494e) or [`MAX`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d4158). Signed right shifts preserve the sign bit.

Decimal [`parse`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a7061727365) rejects trailing bytes and separates invalid syntax from out-of-range input.
Use [`Format`](./format.md#declaration-73696c6b2f666f726d61743a3a466f726d6174) with `Format.display` for defaults or `Format.displayWith` for explicit options.
Both operations stream through a mutable `Writer` without `Allocator`.

## Gotchas

[`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d494e) has no positive i32 counterpart. Use [`wrappingNegate`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a7772617070696e674e6567617465) or [`saturatingNegate`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a73617475726174696e674e6567617465) for its
negation boundary. Use [`checkedDivide`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a636865636b6564446976696465) when division by `-1` can receive [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d494e).

## Examples

### Select an overflow result explicitly

```silk
import silk.i32

import silk.option { Option }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let checked = i32.checkedAdd(i32.MAX, 1)
  let recovered = move checked
    |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(42)
  if i32.wrappingAdd(i32.MAX, 1) != i32.MIN {
    return 1
  }
  if i32.saturatingAdd(i32.MAX, 1) != i32.MAX {
    return 2
  }
  return recovered
}
```

Import as `i32` with `import silk.i32`.

## `negate`

```silk
pub fn negate(value: i32) -> i32
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value` and traps when `value` is [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d494e). Use
this function when that boundary is a program error.

## `wrappingNegate`

```silk
pub fn wrappingNegate(value: i32) -> i32
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value`, wrapped to the `i32` range. [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d494e)
stays [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d494e). Use this function for deliberate modulo arithmetic.

<a id="declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a73617475726174696e674e6567617465"></a>

## `saturatingNegate`

```silk
pub fn saturatingNegate(value: i32) -> i32
```

Returns the arithmetic negation of `value`, clamped to the `i32` range. [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d494e)
becomes [`MAX`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6933323a3a4d4158). Use this function when the positive boundary is required.

## `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse<'life0>(text: string<'life0>) -> silk/result.Result<i32, silk/format.ParseError>
```

Reads the complete text as a signed decimal `i32`.

### Details

A failure contains `silk.format.NotANumber` for empty text, a leading `+`, a non-digit, or
trailing bytes. It contains `silk.format.OutOfRange` if the number is outside the `i32` range.
